reason: Off Vardø: MRS confirmed. Kystverket Barents SRS page states verbatim 'The traffic separation systems off the Norwegian coast from Vardø to Røst are within the operational area of Barents SRS.' SN.1/Circ.318 (MSC.348(91)) para 2.1 points A to H re-read (A/B at 67°10'N; C 68°15'N 009°30'E; D 71°15'N 019°E; E/F 71°50'N; G 71°N 033°20'E). Independent rhumb-line test on Kystverket WFS layer_706 polygons puts every lane and zone polygon landward of the seaward limit (my margins about 8 to 30 nm; small differences from the record's figures do not matter). Norway's national Regulation on vessels' notification obligations (2015 no. 1790) ch.7 ss.19 to 22 also imposes the Barents SRS duty on tankers, hazardous/polluting cargo ships, ships of 5,000 GT and above, etc. in the same Norwegian monitoring area (points a to f identical to MSC.348(91)). VTS dimension: Maritime Traffic Regulations s.6 (Tier 1) lists exactly six VTS areas (Horten, Brevik, Kvitsøy, Fedje, Kinn, Melkøya), and the official s.6 polygons (WFS layer_696) are disjoint from this TSS on re-computation. Kystverket nonetheless describes NOR VTS (Vardø) as providing an 'Information service for Barents SRS and routing schemes (TSS)' and monitoring 'tankers and other risk vessels that follow the routing measures established outside the Norwegian coast', and s.172 gives the NCA a supervisory/intervention role. Under Norway's own regulations that is not a VTS area, so the classification stands, but the coordinator should apply one policy consistently: if shore-based TSS monitoring by a VTS centre outside a declared VTS area is counted, all 19 Norwegian records move up one step (northern to VTS + MRS, southern to VTS only).
